contentHtml:
Do you want to make your own batch of kefir grains to make kefir out of them? Of course, you will have to source the initial culture of grains. I’ve been using kefir grains to make larger batches at home. Let me tell you all about it. But before that, do you know what kefir is?

What is Kefir?

Kefir is a tangy, fermented milk drink that's rich in probiotics. Think of it like a drinkable yoghurt with a unique fizziness and slightly sour taste. People love it for its gut-friendly bacteria that help with digestion and overall health.

Can You Make Kefir Grains from Scratch?

In short, no—you can't generate traditional kefir grains from raw ingredients at home. Kefir grains are the result of centuries of microbial evolution and environmental interaction. While you can ferment milk using a freeze-dried kefir starter culture (sold in packets), the result is usually a drinkable kefir without forming actual grains. These starters are helpful for beginners but will eventually lose potency after a few uses and won’t self-propagate like true kefir grains.

That said, some people attempt to create their own grains by fermenting milk repeatedly with wild-caught cultures or store-bought kefir. While this might lead to thickened, tangy milk and even some sediment, it won’t produce true, reusable kefir grains.

How to Get Reusable Kefir Grains

To make kefir continuously, you’ll need to source real, living kefir grains from someone who already has them. These grains can be purchased online, obtained from local food co-ops, fermentation communities, or even gifted by a fellow home fermenter. Once you have them, simply add them to fresh milk daily. Over time, they will multiply and can be reused indefinitely if properly cared for—making them a sustainable and cost-effective way to keep your kefir flowing.

Kefir starter culture, on the other hand, is made in the lab and is powdered. It has to be dissolved in a small amount of milk before mixing it with the rest of the milk.

Where did Kefir come from?

Kefir has been around for centuries, originating in the Caucasus Mountains of Eastern Europe. Many stories say the shepherds there used to carry milk in leather bags, which fermented into kefir. It’s been a traditional drink in that region for ages.

Using kefir grains or a starter culture to make your kefir is a bit like a science experiment in your kitchen, but don’t worry—it’s simple once you get the hang of it. Follow the steps, let it ferment for a day or two, and voila! You’ll have a delicious, nutritious drink ready to enjoy.

How to Make Kefir Grains?

Ingredients:

  • 1 tablespoon of kefir grains
  • 2 cups of milk (use whole milk for best results)
  • A glass jar or container
  • A breathable cloth or coffee filter
  • Rubber band or string

Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Kefir Grains

  1. Activate the Kefir Grains:

    • Place the kefir grains in a glass jar or container.
    • Pour 2 cups of milk over the grains, ensuring the milk covers the kefir grains completely.

  2. Cover and Ferment:

    • Cover the jar with a muslin cloth or coffee filter, securing it with a rubber band or string.
    • Place the jar in a warm spot, away from direct sunlight, for 24-48 hours.

  3. Strain and Rinse:

    • After 24-48 hours, the milk should have thickened and developed a slightly sour taste.
    • Strain the kefir grains through a sieve or strainer to separate them from the kefir.

  4. Rinse and Repeat:

    • Rinse the kefir grains gently under cold water to remove any milk residue.
    • Place the kefir grains back into the glass jar and repeat the process with fresh milk.

  5. Storage and Maintenance:

    • Store the kefir grains in the refrigerator in milk when you are not using it.
    • To keep the grains active, repeat the fermentation process regularly. This will ensure they remain active and productive.

Nutrition Facts of Kefir (per 100 ml):

  • Calories: 50
  • Carbohydrates: 5g
  • Protein: 3g
  • Fat: 2g
  • Calcium: 10% DV

Health Benefits of Kefir:

  • Probiotic-Rich: Kefir contains a variety of beneficial bacteria and yeasts that support gut health.
  • Nutrient Dense: Packed with vitamins (K2), minerals (calcium) and protein, kefir is a nutritious addition to your diet.
  • Digestive Aid: Helps improve digestion and may boost immune function.

Fun Fact: Did you know that kefir is low in lactose? The lactic acid bacteria in kefir digest the lactose. If you have lactose intolerance, you can enjoy kefir. You can also make kefir from coconut water for a vegan kefir.

How to Store Kefir Grains?

  1. Short-Term Storage (Up to 1 Week – Refrigeration)

• Place the kefir grains in a jar with fresh milk (enough to fully submerge them).

• Seal the jar loosely and store it in the fridge.

• Change the milk every 5–7 days to keep the grains alive.

  1. Long-Term Storage (Freezing Up to 3 Months)

  • Rinse the grains gently with filtered water (optional).
  • Pat dry with a clean paper towel and place in an airtight container or freezer bag.
  • Add a small amount of dry milk powder to protect them.
  • Store in the freezer. To revive, thaw and place in fresh milk at room temperature.

  1. Dehydration (Up to 6 Months or More)

  • Rinse the grains and spread them on parchment paper or a dehydrator tray.
  • Let them air-dry at room temperature for 3 days or use a dehydrator at a very low temperature (not above 40°C).
  • Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place or refrigerate.
  • To reactivate, soak in fresh milk and refresh daily until fermentation restarts.

Troubleshooting Tips for Kefir Grains

If your kefir grains are not fermenting properly, here are common issues and solutions to restore their health.

1. Kefir is Too Thin (Not Thickening)

a. Possible Causes:

  1. Low grain-to-milk ratio
  2. Cold fermentation environment
  3. Weak or inactive grains

b. Solutions:

  • Increase the kefir grains (1 tbsp per 1 cup of milk).
  • Place the jar in a warmer spot (20-25°C).
  • Refresh with fresh milk every 12-24 hours until fermentation improves.

2. Kefir Smells Off (Rotten, Mouldy, or Extra Sour)

a. Possible Causes:

  1. Over-fermentation (left too long)
  2. Dirty or contaminated jar
  3. Poor-quality or old milk

b. Solutions:

  • Reduce fermentation time to 12-18 hours.
  • Use a clean glass jar and filtered water to rinse grains (if needed).
  • Try fresh, high-quality whole milk.

3. Kefir Grains are Not Growing or Multiplying

a. Possible Causes:

  1. Overcrowding (too many grains in one jar)
  2. Poor milk quality (ultra-pasteurised or non-dairy milk)
  3. Grains are weak from improper storage

b. Solutions:

  • Separate large clusters and ferment in smaller batches.
  • Use fresh, full-fat dairy milk.
  • Feed grains regularly and avoid refrigeration for too long.

4. Kefir Grains Look Slimy or Disintegrate

a. Possible Causes:

  • Too much exposure to acidic kefir (not strained in time)
  • Inconsistent feeding schedule
  • Contaminated grains

b. Solutions:

  • Strain kefir on time (every 12â€“24 hours).
  • Keep a consistent feeding cycle with fresh milk.
  • If grains turn mushy, rinse with filtered water and restart in fresh milk.

5. Kefir Separates into Curd and Whey Too Fast

a. Possible Causes:

  1. Over-fermentation
  2. Too much heat
  3. Too many grains in too little milk

b. Solutions:

  • Reduce fermentation time or place in a cooler spot.
  • Stir gently before straining to mix curds and whey.
  • Adjust the grain-to-milk ratio (use more milk or fewer grains).

Final Tip:

If kefir grains stop working after multiple attempts, try refreshing them with a sugar-water soak (for water kefir) or fresh raw milk (for milk kefir) for a few days before resuming fermentation.

Commonly Asked Questions about Kefir Grains

Q: Is kefir dairy-free? Traditional kefir is made from dairy milk, but you can make dairy-free versions using oat milk, almond milk, or other plant-based alternatives.

Q: What are the health benefits of kefir? Kefir is rich in probiotics that support gut health, boost immunity, and help digestion. Furthermore, it provides essential nutrients like calcium, protein, and vitamins.

Q: How do I make kefir at home? To make kefir, combine kefir grains with milk (or a non-dairy alternative), let it ferment for 24-48 hours, then strain and refrigerate.

Q: Can I drink kefir every day? Yes, drinking kefir daily can be beneficial for maintaining a healthy gut microbiome and overall digestive health. Start with a small quantity like 25-50 ml.

Q: How can I flavor kefir? You can flavour kefir by adding fruits, honey, or spices like cinnamon. You can add the flavors after fermentation. Try different combinations to suit your taste.

Q: How long does kefir last in the refrigerator? Properly stored, kefir can last up to 1 week. The taste may become tangier over time.

Q: Can I freeze kefir? Freezing kefir can affect the texture and probiotic content. It's best enjoyed fresh or refrigerated.

Making kefir grains from scratch is a simple and rewarding process that allows you to enjoy the benefits of homemade kefir. Experiment with different types of milk and fermentation times to customize your kefir to your taste preferences.

Healthy Kefir Recipes

1. Probiotic-Packed Mango Kefir Smoothie for Gut Health

Boost your digestive health with this creamy and delicious mango kefir smoothie. Combining the benefits of probiotic-rich kefir and nutrient-packed mangoes, this smoothie is perfect for improving gut health and supporting your immune system.

Ingredients for Kefir Smoothie:

  • 1 cup of plain kefir
  • 1 ripe mango, peeled and chopped
  • 1 tablespoon honey (optional)
  • 1/2 cup ice cubes
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric (optional for added anti-inflammatory benefits)

Instructions:

  1. In a blender, combine kefir, mango, honey, and ice cubes.
  2. Blend until smooth and creamy.
  3. Pour into a glass, and sprinkle a pinch of turmeric for an extra health boost.
  4. Enjoy this probiotic-packed drink to promote a healthy gut and improve digestion!

Benefits: This recipe is perfect for boosting your gut health and improving digestion, thanks to the probiotic power of kefir.

2. Simple Kefir and Berry Breakfast Parfait for Weight Loss

Start your day with a nutrient-dense kefir and berry breakfast parfait, ideal for those looking to manage their weight while enjoying a flavorful, satisfying meal. Packed with antioxidants from fresh berries and protein from kefir, this parfait makes for a delicious and healthy breakfast option.

Ingredients:

  • 1/2 cup plain kefir
  • 1/2 cup mixed berries (blueberries, strawberries, raspberries)
  • 1/4 cup rolled oats
  • 1 tablespoon chia seeds
  • 1 teaspoon maple syrup (optional)

Instructions:

  1. Layer the oats, kefir, and berries in a glass or bowl.
  2. Top with chia seeds and drizzle with maple syrup for sweetness.
  3. Refrigerate for 30 minutes for the oats to soften.
  4. Enjoy this filling and nutritious parfait to kickstart your day while supporting your weight management goals.

Benefits: With probiotics from kefir and the nutritional benefits of berries, this recipe aids in weight management while providing lasting energy.
